summary: Most automated writing feedback relies on cloud-hosted LLMs, which raises data privacy concerns for students and young authors; Local Quill is a local feedback system that keeps all user data on-device
The project focuses on academic essays and fictional prose, aimed at students and aspiring authors
It uses local models of about 8 billion parameters, supported by RAG over writing guides and style manuals, and splits feedback into grammar, clarity and style sub-tasks with separate prompts
The research question asks whether such a local solution with RAG can achieve results comparable to GPT-5-nano, measured by G-Eval metrics
arguments: Cloud-hosted models risk that submitted text is retained or used for training by third parties, so a local, on-device system is needed
Small local models have smaller context windows, weaker instruction following and lower output quality, but RAG grounds their answers with field-specific knowledge from writing guides
Splitting feedback into separate grammar, clarity and style prompts lets each call specialise and gives more targeted feedback than one combined prompt
Training an LLM from scratch is beyond student projects, but pretrained models are suited for zero-shot tasks; the most capable ones are only available in the cloud
arguments_main: Names data privacy (keeping user data on-device instead of sending it to cloud providers) as the most important argument
Gives a reason from the text, e.g. it is the motivation for the whole project and the gap Local Quill targets
